title: Code-switched answer with a real misconception
label: Demo data — synthetic
question: If a function is continuous at a sharp corner like |x| at 0, is it differentiable there?
student_answer: Yes na, once the line continuous and no break dey inside, sharpness no matter at all, so differentiation must work sharp sharp.

chunks.text: Continuity does not guarantee differentiability. A sharp corner or cusp causes left and right derivative slopes to disagree, meaning the derivative does not exist.
